I farm only 5 mu, and my land is in a wheat-maize rotation with well irrigation, so I will keep the system simple, steady, and low-risk. Because some people in my family work off-farm, I will not choose anything that needs too much labor or fine management. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on enough nitrogen with moderate phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to the times that usually matter most. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me more stable yield on small land, and after wheat harvest I will move fast and use no-tillage so I do not lose moisture or time. I will rely on the well for two irrigations in each crop if rainfall is not enough. I am not chasing the highest possible yield; I am trying to get a dependable harvest from the land I have with labor I can manage.
